claims.text: The unmodified AlCoCrFeNi2.1-type alloy has a dual-phase FCC/B2 lamellar-colony microstructure.
Internal boundaries in the unmodified lamellar colonies are prone to microcrack initiation during room-temperature tensile deformation.
The unmodified alloy has high strength but limited room-temperature tensile ductility because of microcrack initiation at internal boundaries.
Adding approximately 0.5 at% Hf will improve the alloy's mechanical behavior.
Approximately 0.5 at% Hf will cause in situ formation of fine Hf-rich precipitates.
The Hf-rich precipitates will selectively form along internal lamellar phase boundaries or colony interfaces.
Fine Hf-rich precipitates will act as pinning agents at the internal boundaries.
Hf-rich boundary precipitates will enhance interfacial cohesion.
The Hf-rich precipitates will retard microcrack initiation at internal interfaces.
The Hf-rich precipitates will retard propagation of microcracks along internal interfaces.
Suppressing interfacial microcracking will promote effective load transfer during tensile deformation.
The precipitates will provide additional energy-dissipation paths during tensile straining.
The Hf-added alloy will have a higher room-temperature yield strength than the unmodified alloy.
The Hf-added alloy will have a higher room-temperature ultimate tensile strength than the unmodified alloy.
The Hf-added alloy will have greater room-temperature elongation to failure than the unmodified alloy.
The simultaneous strength and ductility benefit exists only within a narrow Hf-concentration window.
Excessive Hf can produce large or continuous intermetallic phases that embrittle the alloy.
Retention of the characteristic lamellar microstructure is required for the proposed mechanism to be effective.

contradictions.description: The boundary condition predicts that excessive Hf may form coarse or continuous embrittling phases, but the falsification rule broadly treats formation of such phases by an Hf addition as falsifying the hypothesis. Thus, an expected failure at an out-of-window composition such as 0.8 at% could incorrectly falsify a hypothesis that only asserts benefit within a narrow window.
